episode.whitechapel_1888.title: Whitechapel, 1888
whitechapel_1888.clock.look: The mantel clock stopped at twenty to four. 3:40. Nobody has wound it since. Nobody dares.
whitechapel_1888.clippings.look: Five newspaper clippings, pinned oldest first: [[bucks_row]]. [[hanbury_street]]. [[berner_street]]. [[mitre_square]]. [[millers_court]]. The headlines give him a name. Theirs are only in the small print.
whitechapel_1888.letter.unfolded: Inside, a crude map: five streets in brown ink, a pin pushed through each, and a length of red wool tied to the first.
episode.whitechapel_1888.teaser: A rented room, a stopped clock, and five names the fog has kept.
whitechapel_1888.bed.look: The bed is made, as if someone meant to come back tonight. The pillow is still cold.
whitechapel_1888.candles.cold: Five candles, each with a street name scratched into the brass. Cold. You'll need a flame.
whitechapel_1888.candles.lit: Five small flames, standing very still. The room seems to breathe a little easier.
whitechapel_1888.candles.solved: One by one the wicks catch. Somewhere a church bell answers. Tucked beneath the candlesticks: a card with a name.
whitechapel_1888.hearth.look: Ash, long gone grey. Something was burned here: paper, by the look of it. Too much of it.
whitechapel_1888.door.locked: Locked from the other side. The wood is damp with fog. Whatever holds this room shut is not a key.
whitechapel_1888.door.leave: The door gives way. Outside there is no street, only the soft grey of the jar, and the shelf beyond. Behind you, five candles go on burning.
whitechapel_1888.coat.pocket: A heavy wool coat, still smelling of rain. In the pocket, a lens without its frame.
whitechapel_1888.coat.look: Empty pockets. Whoever wore this walked these streets every night that autumn.
whitechapel_1888.frames.restored: Five names where there were none, each under its date, from [[aug31]] to [[nov09]]: [[nichols]], [[chapman]], [[stride]], [[eddowes]], [[kelly]]. They look back at you: not as headlines, but as women.
whitechapel_1888.frames.solved: Under each frame, in your own hand: [[nichols]]. [[chapman]]. [[stride]]. [[eddowes]]. [[kelly]]. Five names, five places. Somewhere behind you, a lock turns.
whitechapel_1888.faded_paper.look: A page so faded it's nearly blank. There's writing here, too small and too pale to read by eye.
whitechapel_1888.faded_paper.read: Under the glass, a line of ink comes back: a lodging-house register, and one name, written carefully. Mary Jane Kelly.
whitechapel_1888.drawer.empty: Only the smell of old paper now.
whitechapel_1888.drawer.opened: The drawer slides open with a sigh. A box of matches, a folded letter, and a card with a name.
whitechapel_1888.street_map.done: A red thread runs through five streets, oldest first. The fog on the glass has thinned, just a little.
whitechapel_1888.street_map.solved: The thread pulls taut through the last pin. Two cards slip from behind the map: two names from the same night.
whitechapel_1888.fog.look: Fog presses against the glass, thick as wool. Somewhere in it, a gas lamp. Somewhere, footsteps that never come closer.
item.whitechapel_1888.matches.desc: Safety matches, the box half full. Enough for five small flames.
item.whitechapel_1888.matches.name: Box of matches
item.whitechapel_1888.letter.desc: Addressed to no one. The ink has run in the damp. It's folded more times than it needs to be.
item.whitechapel_1888.letter.name: Folded letter
item.whitechapel_1888.lens.desc: A small round lens. It needs something to hold it.
item.whitechapel_1888.lens.name: Loose lens
item.whitechapel_1888.brass_frame.desc: A tiny brass ring with a handle, its glass long gone.
item.whitechapel_1888.brass_frame.name: Brass frame
item.whitechapel_1888.magnifier.desc: Lens and frame, together again. Small things become legible.
item.whitechapel_1888.magnifier.name: Magnifying glass
item.whitechapel_1888.name_card_stride.d: [[stride]]. Found in [[berner_street]], 30 September 1888, around one in the morning.
[[eddowes]]. Found in [[mitre_square]], 30 September 1888, less than an hour later.
hint.whitechapel_1888.light_candles.1: The candles on the mantel are cold. You carry something that could change that.
hint.whitechapel_1888.light_candles.2: Select the matches, then tap the candles.
hint.whitechapel_1888.open_drawer.1: The desk drawer is locked with a small clock face. Time matters in this room.
hint.whitechapel_1888.open_drawer.2: The clock on the mantel stopped at a certain time.
hint.whitechapel_1888.open_drawer.3: Set the drawer's clock to 3:40: the hour hand on III, the minute hand on VIII.
hint.whitechapel_1888.find_names.1: The room is keeping something. Look closely at everything that was left behind.
hint.whitechapel_1888.find_names.2: There are five empty frames on the west wall. Each one is waiting for a name.
hint.whitechapel_1888.desk_drawer.1: A clock for a lock. Something in this room stopped and never started again.
hint.whitechapel_1888.desk_drawer.2: Read the time on the mantel clock, and set these hands to it.
hint.whitechapel_1888.desk_drawer.3: Hour hand on III, minute hand on VIII: twenty to four.
episode.test_room.title: Test room
episode.lawang_sewu_1945.title: Semarang, 1945
episode.lawang_sewu_1945.teaser: A thousand doors, a stopped clock, and five lockers left empty.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.stairs: The grand staircase climbs into the dark. Every step is worn in the middle, by thousands of feet that no longer come.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.glass_dark: The great stained-glass window is dark, as if the light behind it had been told to wait.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.clock_running: The station clock ticks again. Somewhere far below, a train is late for a platform that is no longer there.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.clock_solved: The hands shiver and move on. Behind the clock, a little door swings open.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.lantern: A railwayman's lantern, cold and dry. Its wick is waiting for oil.
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.glass_solved: Light returns to the glass: the plants and animals of Java, the cities of Semarang and Batavia, the winged wheel between fire and water. The whole building draws a breath.
lawang_sewu_1945.ending.battle: And the building remembers October 1945. Five days, from the 15th to the 19th: the Battle of Five Days in Semarang. The young railway workers of AMKA held the square across the road, Wilhelminaplein. Many did not come home, on both sides.
lawang_sewu_1945.ending.tugu: Across that road, one day, Tugu Muda will stand. Here, five lockers are no longer empty. One by one, all nine hundred and twenty-eight doors close, gently.
lawang_sewu_1945.corridor.endless: Door after door after door. The corridor goes on further than the building should allow.
lawang_sewu_1945.corridor.door_1945_lock: A door marked 1945. It won't open. From behind it, very faintly, a telegraph is clicking, waiting for an answer.
lawang_sewu_1945.corridor.locker_door_op: The lock turns. Beyond the door: a small room of iron lockers.
lawang_sewu_1945.office.telegram_form: A telegram form, filled in and never sent: "Reply with this office's signature: the company's three initials."
lawang_sewu_1945.office.timetable_solved: The plates settle into their proper order and the station bell rings once. In the tray below: a conductor's ticket punch.
lawang_sewu_1945.office.timetable_done: The first line of the Indies, in its right order. Twenty-six kilometres that changed Java.
lawang_sewu_1945.office.telegraph_solved: N. I. S. The line crackles, and far away a door unlocks. The telegraphist's key comes loose in your hand.
lawang_sewu_1945.office.telegraph_done: The telegraph is silent now. The message was received.
lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.page_0: The ledger of the Nederlandsch-Indische Spoorweg Maatschappij. A hand-drawn map: the first railway line in the Indies, opened on 10 August [[year_1867]]. [[samarang]], then [[alastua]], then [[brumbung]], then [[tanggung]].
lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.page_1: A telegraphist's crib sheet, in pencil. N is dash, dot. I is dot, dot. S is dot, dot, dot. The rest of the alphabet has been rubbed away.
lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.page_2: Building plans, by the firm of Klinkhamer and Ouëndag. In the margin, a clerk's note: "They will call it the thousand doors. I counted them myself: [[doors_928]]."
lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.page_3: A description of the stained glass, made in [[delft]] by J.L. Schouten: Java's plants and animals, the cities of Semarang and [[batavia]], and a winged wheel where Fortuna's fire meets Venus's water, and becomes steam. A clerk has added: "When fire and water both stand at the top, the wheel turns."
lawang_sewu_1945.window.outside: Smoke over the square across the road. Somewhere, church bells, and under them a sound like distant rain that is not rain.
lawang_sewu_1945.window.calendar: A wall calendar, never torn again after that day: Monday, [[date_15oct]].
lawang_sewu_1945.window.cap: A young railway driver's cap, left on the sill as if its owner meant to come back for it.
lawang_sewu_1945.cellar.dark: Black water, black arches. You can hear the dripping, but you can't see your own hand.
lawang_sewu_1945.cellar.lit: The lantern pushes the dark back to the walls. The cellar is knee-deep in still water.
lawang_sewu_1945.cellar.tally: Scratches on the wall, in groups of five. Someone counted the days here. The counting stops.
lawang_sewu_1945.cellar.chair: A single wooden chair, facing the wall. During the occupation this basement was a prison. Nobody sits in the chair now.
lawang_sewu_1945.cellar.whistle: Something glints under the water: a stationmaster's whistle. It is still cold.
lawang_sewu_1945.lockers.solved: Five lockers, five small things returned. In October 1945, [[five]] employees of this building did not come back. Their lockers are no longer empty.
lawang_sewu_1945.lockers.done: Each locker holds what its owner left behind: the things of [[five]] people who did not come home.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.name: Ledger
item.lawang_sewu_1945.ledger.desc: The office ledger. Tap the left page to read, the right edge to turn.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lamp_oil.name: Lamp oil
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lamp_oil.desc: A small tin of lamp oil, still sloshing.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lantern.name: Lantern
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lantern.desc: A railwayman's lantern, dry. It needs oil.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lit_lantern.name: Lit lantern
item.lawang_sewu_1945.lit_lantern.desc: The shunter's lantern, burning. Shunters swung these to guide trains in the dark.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.ticket_punch.name: Ticket punch
item.lawang_sewu_1945.ticket_punch.desc: The conductor's ticket punch. A crumb of old ticket is still caught in its jaws.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.telegraph_key.name: Telegraph key
item.lawang_sewu_1945.telegraph_key.desc: The telegraphist's key, worn smooth by one thumb.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.driver_cap.name: Driver's cap
item.lawang_sewu_1945.driver_cap.desc: A young driver's cap, soot on the brim.
item.lawang_sewu_1945.whistle.name: Whistle
item.lawang_sewu_1945.whistle.desc: The stationmaster's whistle. It sent a thousand trains away.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.read_the_ledger.1: The building keeps records. Look for the office behind the door marked 1907.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.read_the_ledger.2: Read every page of the ledger on the desk. Each one answers a door somewhere.
The telegram form asks for a reply. The telegraph is on the desk.
The company's name heads the first page of the ledger; the second page tells you how to tap it.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.set_the_clock.1: The clock on the landing wants a day and a month.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.set_the_clock.2: Which day did the calendar in 1945 stop on?
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.light_the_cellar.1: The lantern is dry. Something in the 1907 office could fill it.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.light_the_cellar.2: Combine the lantern with the lamp oil, then use it on the darkness behind the door marked 1942.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.open_the_lockers.1: The locker room door needs three digits. The building's nickname is not quite true.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.open_the_lockers.2: Someone counted the doors. The ledger's third page says how many.
You carry five things that belong to five people. Their lockers are waiting.
Examine each item: its description names the job of the person who owned it.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.light_the_glass.1: The lockers are full. Now the great window on the landing.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.light_the_glass.2: The last page of the ledger explains the glass.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.timetable.1: Four station plates, out of order. They belong to one line.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.timetable.2: The ledger's first page has a map of the first line, from Semarang outward.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.telegraph.1: Three letters. Short and long taps.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.telegraph.2: The company: Nederlandsch-Indische Spoorweg. Its initials, in the Morse code from the ledger.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.telegraph.3: N-I-S: dash, dot, then dot, dot, then dot, dot, dot.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.station_clock.1: Two small windows: a day and a month.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.station_clock.2: The calendar behind the door marked 1945 never moved past one day.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.locker_door.1: Three digits. How many doors does a thousand doors really have?
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.locker_door.2: A clerk counted them, in the ledger's third page.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.lockers.1: Each locker has a job on its plate.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.lockers.2: Examine the items: each description names its owner's job.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.lockers.3: Cap: driver. Ticket punch: conductor. Key: telegraphist. Lantern: shunter. Whistle: stationmaster.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.stained_glass.1: Three rings of glass. Each one has a mark.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.stained_glass.2: All marks must stand at the top. Turning a ring also turns the one inside it.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.stained_glass.3: Turn the outer ring 5 times, then the middle ring 5 times, then the inner ring 5 times.
whitechapel_1888.fog.wiped: Someone wrote in the fog, from the inside, in a careful hand: [[berner_street]] — [[mitre_square]]. One night. Not an hour apart.
whitechapel_1888.keeper.note: A scrap the fire would not take, in a careful hand: "I burned every paper that gave him a name. Theirs I kept, in the small print, where no one looks. Whoever keeps this room after me: keep them too."
hint.whitechapel_1888.write_label.1: You carry five names now. The frames on the west wall are waiting, dated from the first to the last.
hint.whitechapel_1888.write_label.2: Every word you need is underlined somewhere: on the cards, in the clippings, in the fog on the window. Tap it to note it.
hint.whitechapel_1888.find_names.3: Underlined words in what you read can be noted: tap them. You will need them before you leave.
hint.whitechapel_1888.jar_label.1: The label asks for two names: who came first, and who came last.
hint.whitechapel_1888.jar_label.2: The first was found in Buck's Row on 31 August; the last, indoors, in Miller's Court on 9 November.
hint.whitechapel_1888.jar_label.3: Mary Ann Nichols; Mary Jane Kelly.
hint.whitechapel_1888.window_fog.1: The glass is fogged from the inside. Wipe it.
hint.whitechapel_1888.window_fog.2: Drag your finger back and forth across the middle of the pane.
hint.whitechapel_1888.hearth_ash.1: Brush the ash aside with your finger. Something did not burn.
lawang_sewu_1945.corridor.door_929: Past the last door there is one more, smaller, with no year on it. Only a number: 929. A note is pinned to it, in a careful hand: "The building added a door the night I came. I never opened it. Whoever keeps this room after me: don't."
lawang_sewu_1945.landing.label_needed: The light waits in the glass. Below it, a paper label for the jar, still blank.
lawang_sewu_1945.label.s1: They called it a thousand doors, but there are {1}.
lawang_sewu_1945.label.s2: On {1} the fighting began across the square, and {2} of its workers did not come home.
lawang_sewu_1945.label.done: The telegram is written out in a clerk's careful hand. The building reads it, and remembers the rest.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.write_label.1: The glass is lit, but the jar still needs its label. Tap the glass again.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.write_label.2: The ledger holds most of the words; the calendar and the lockers hold the rest. Tap underlined words to note them.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.jar_label.1: The ledger counts the doors; the calendar knows the day.
hint.lawang_sewu_1945.jar_label.2: Not a thousand. The calendar stopped on the day the fighting began; the lockers tell you how many did not come home.
episode.flannan_isles_1900.title: Flannan Isles, 1900
episode.flannan_isles_1900.teaser: A dark lamp, a stopped clock, and one oilskin left on its hook.
flannan_isles_1900.east.plaque: A brass plaque by the gate: NORTHERN LIGHTHOUSE BOARD · FLANNAN ISLANDS · FIRST LIT 7 · XII · 1899.
flannan_isles_1900.east.gate_open: The latch is stiff with salt, but it lifts. The gate swings in on a yard where nothing moves.
flannan_isles_1900.east.flagpole: The flagpole is bare. A keeper would have run up a flag to greet the relief. No one did.
flannan_isles_1900.east.boat: Far below, the relief boat rides the swell at [[east_landing]], where you came up, her lamps smeared by fog. She has sounded her horn again and again. No one has come down.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.store_dark: The oil store has no window. Inside it is black as pitch. You will need a light.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.tower_dark: The tower door opens on a stair that spirals up into complete darkness.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.path_blocked: The path west runs off into the dark. Something lies across it, but you cannot make out what; beyond, only the sound of the sea.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.tower: The tower stands over the island, twenty-three metres of stone. Its lamp should have been lit at dusk. It is dark.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.tower_lit: The beam sweeps out over the sea, and back, and out again. In its light the path west shows plain.
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.clock: The clock on the wall has stopped. No one was here to wind it.
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.stove: The stove is cold. No fire has been lit for days.
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.table: The table is bare and scrubbed; the dishes are washed and put away. Whatever happened here, it did not happen at a meal.
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.log: The station log. On duty: [[ducat]], [[marshall]] and [[mcarthur]]. The last entries are signed by the Principal Keeper, J. Ducat, and run up to [[date_13dec]]. In the margin: "D. McArthur, Occasional Keeper, in place of W. Ross, on sick leave."
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.slate: The slate by the door, where readings were chalked before being copied into the log. The last ones — barometer, thermometer, wind — were taken at [[time_9am]] on [[date_15dec]].
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.hooks: Three hooks by the door, tagged Principal, Second Assistant, Occasional. Two are empty, and two pairs of seaboots are gone. Only the Occasional Keeper's oilskin still hangs here: he went out without it, in his [[shirtsleeves]].
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.magazine: On the shelf, a magazine that should not be here yet: 1912. A poem about this room, with [[chair]] and [[meal]] on the table, as if the keepers had fled in the middle of supper. The real table is clean.
flannan_isles_1900.store.cans: Cans of paraffin for the great lamp, stacked in rows. Enough light for a whole winter.
flannan_isles_1900.stair.door_locked: At the top of the stair, the door to the lamp room is locked.
flannan_isles_1900.stair.door_opened: The key turns. Above, the lamp room is grey with the last of the evening.
flannan_isles_1900.stair.hook_note: In the dark, a fourth hook, with no name on its tag. A note is tucked behind it, in a careful hand: "Three hooks for the keepers of the light, and one for whoever keeps their names. I hung my coat here once."
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.lamp: The lamp is clean, the wicks trimmed, the fountain full of oil: ready for a night that never came.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.need_wind: A lit lamp must turn, or the great lens would burn one spot of sea all night. Wind the clockwork first.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.full: The fountain is already full. The keepers saw to that.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.lit: The wick takes the flame. The lens begins to turn, and the beam goes out over the sea for the first time in eleven nights.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.clockwork: The clockwork that turns the lens has run down. The winding handle is not on its peg.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.clockwork_wound: The weights climb and the gears take up the strain. The lens is ready to turn.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.clockwork_done: The clockwork ticks steadily, turning the lens.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.legend_log: Pages pinned by the lens, in a hand that is no keeper's: a great storm, the men weeping and praying, then calm. None of it was ever in the real log. Someone wrote [[storm_log]] years later, and the story believed it.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.label_needed: Beneath the lens hangs the jar's label, still blank. The light is back; now the truth must be written down.
flannan_isles_1900.west.railings: This is [[west_landing]]. Its iron railings are twisted like wire, and the rails of the tramway are torn out of their concrete.
flannan_isles_1900.west.rope_box: The plate reads ROPES AND TACKLE. The box it marked was kept in a crevice thirty-three metres above the water, and it is gone. The sea came higher than that.
flannan_isles_1900.west.turf: At the very top of the cliff, more than sixty metres above the sea, the turf has been torn away.
flannan_isles_1900.west.crane: The landing crane still stands. Whatever came here came as water.
flannan_isles_1900.label.s1: On {1}, the sea at {2} took all three; {3} ran after the others in his shirtsleeves.
flannan_isles_1900.label.done: The label is written: the day, the place, and the man who ran after the others. The legend can stay in its magazine.
flannan_isles_1900.ending.light: The lamp turns, and the Flannan light shines again. Out in the fog, the relief boat answers with her horn.
flannan_isles_1900.ending.names: James Ducat. Thomas Marshall. Donald McArthur. Keepers of this light, taken by the sea on 15 December 1900. The relief lit it again that night; since 1971 it has kept itself. It is still turning.
item.flannan_isles_1900.matches.name: Box of matches
item.flannan_isles_1900.matches.desc: Kitchen matches, dry in their box.
item.flannan_isles_1900.hand_lantern.des: A keeper's hand lantern, trimmed and filled. It needs a flame.
item.flannan_isles_1900.lit_lantern.name: Lit lantern
item.flannan_isles_1900.lit_lantern.desc: A small, steady flame behind glass. Enough to see a step or two in the dark.
item.flannan_isles_1900.paraffin.name: Can of paraffin
item.flannan_isles_1900.paraffin.desc: A heavy can of paraffin for the great lamp.
item.flannan_isles_1900.crank_handle.des: An iron handle with a wooden grip, made to wind a clockwork.
item.flannan_isles_1900.lamp_key.name: Lamp-room key
item.flannan_isles_1900.lamp_key.desc: A heavy key on a brass tag: LAMP ROOM.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.open_gate.1: The light is up the steps, through the gate in the wall.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.open_gate.2: Tap the gate and lift its latch.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.light_lantern.1: The living quarters are through the door on the left. Keepers kept a light by the door.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.light_lantern.2: Take the lantern from beside the hooks and the matches from the stove, and put them together.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.climb_tower.1: With a light you can go where it is dark: the oil store and the tower stair.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.climb_tower.2: Drag your finger to move the lantern. Look for a handle in the store and a key on the stair.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.wind_clockwork.1: The lamp cannot be lit until the lens can turn.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.wind_clockwork.2: Use the winding handle on the clockwork, then turn it round and round.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.light_lamp.1: The lens is wound. The lamp only needs a flame.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.light_lamp.2: Use the lit lantern on the lamp.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.go_west.1: The beam showed you what blocks the path west.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.go_west.2: In the yard, tap the path west to drag the rail aside.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.write_label.1: The label hangs beneath the lens. Tap the lamp.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.write_label.2: The label tells it the legend's way. Correct the day, the place, and the man who ran after the others.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.clockwork.1: Drag the handle round in a circle.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.clockwork.2: Keep turning clockwise until the ring is full.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.jar_label.1: The label tells it the legend's way. On which day did the readings on the slate stop?
hint.flannan_isles_1900.jar_label.2: Which landing did the sea come up, and who ran after the others?
hint.flannan_isles_1900.jar_label.3: 15 December 1900; the west landing; Donald McArthur.
episode.pompeii_79.title: Pompeii, 79
episode.pompeii_79.teaser: A sealed oven, an empty house, and a lens that remembers the afternoon the mountain woke.
pompeii_79.street.vesuvius: Vesuvius, beyond the rooftops that are no longer there. A thin thread of smoke still rises from it. It has not finished.
pompeii_79.street.plaque: A board on a post, lettered by the diggers: EXCAVATIONS OF POMPEII · BEGUN [[year_1748]]. Under it, newer paint: REGIO VII.
pompeii_79.street.notice: Red paint on the plaster, half flaked away: an election notice. The bakers ask you to vote for their man. You can make out little more.
pompeii_79.street.ruts: The paving stones are worn into two deep grooves by cart wheels. Stepping stones cross the street, so no one had to wade.
pompeii_79.street.ash_bank: The shop's doorway is buried to the chest in grey ash, set hard as mortar. The diggers have not got this far.
pompeii_79.street.dug: The ash gives way. Behind it, the shop door stands open, the way it was left.
pompeii_79.hut.town_plan: A plan of the city, the gates marked in ink: [[vesuvius_gate]] to the north, facing the mountain; [[marina_gate]] to the west, down towards the sea; and the Stabian, Nucerian, Sarno, Nolan, and Herculaneum gates.
pompeii_79.hut.pliny: The letters of Pliny the Younger, who watched from across the bay. The cloud rose "like [[pine_tree]]", a tall trunk spreading into branches. People fled with [[pillows]] tied on their heads against the falling stones. A note in the margin: the old manuscripts give the day as [[august_24]].
pompeii_79.hut.guidebook: A traveller's guidebook: "Pompeii, swallowed by [[lava]] in a single instant, its people frozen where they stood." Beside it, someone has written in pencil: No.
pompeii_79.hut.daybook: The diggers' day-book, [[year_1863]]. "The baker's house: empty. The strongbox locked, and no key to it; the household gods gone. In the garden, above the pumice, hollows in the hard ash in the shape of people. We filled them with plaster, as Director Fiorelli showed us. We do not know who they were."
pompeii_79.hut.crate: A crate of finds, each wrapped in straw and tagged: a lamp, three coins, a bronze ladle, a child's knucklebones.
pompeii_79.hut.table: The draughtsman's table. A sheet of squared paper is pinned down, with a small cross at each corner, waiting for something to be laid over it.
pompeii_79.hut.table_done: The four tracings lie pinned together: a boat, three figures, a gate, and AD MARE.
pompeii_79.hut.lens: A brass lens on a handle, left on the plan. Through it the ash is not there yet: the house as it was, the afternoon the mountain woke. (Raise it with the lens at the bottom left; drag to look around.)
pompeii_79.hut.tracings_done: The crosses meet, and four sheets become one drawing, in a child's hand: a boat on the waves; three figures walking towards it, [[pillows]] tied on their heads; a gate, with the sea beyond it; and two words, AD MARE. To the sea.
pompeii_79.bakery.mills: Two millstones of grey lava stone, shaped like hourglasses. A donkey walked round and round to turn them. The ring its hooves wore in the floor is still there.
pompeii_79.bakery.oven_stuck: The oven's iron door is jammed shut with ash. Something to lever it would do.
pompeii_79.bakery.oven_opened: The door grinds open. Inside, the oven is still full.
pompeii_79.bakery.loaves: Round loaves of [[bread]], black as coal, each scored into eight. Each was pressed with a stamp, but the fire has taken the letters.
pompeii_79.bakery.store: Tall jars sunk in the floor, still sealed: the new wine, put away after the harvest. On the shelf, pomegranates and chestnuts, charred black. [[autumn]] fruit.
pompeii_79.atrium.shrine: The household shrine: a painted niche with two serpents and an altar. The little bronze gods that stood here are gone. Whoever left took them.
pompeii_79.atrium.drawing: A drawing in charcoal, low on the wall, where a child could reach. Most of it has flaked away. The diggers' draughtsman must have traced it before it went.
pompeii_79.atrium.graffito: Scratched into the plaster, in a grown-up hand: "I am amazed, O wall, that you have not fallen in ruins, you who hold up the scribbles of so many writers." The same joke is on walls all over the city.
pompeii_79.atrium.crack: A long crack from the great earthquake of 62, patched with fresh plaster. Seventeen years on, the repairs were still not finished.
pompeii_79.atrium.basin: The rainwater basin in the floor is full to the brim with pale stones, light as sponge.
pompeii_79.atrium.tracings: A tin tube, dropped by the wall. Inside, four sheets of tracing paper: the draughtsman's copies of the drawing, in pieces.
pompeii_79.atrium.toy_found: In the niche under the stair, packed in ash, a little clay horse on wheels. The diggers missed it. It has been waiting here since the afternoon it was hidden.
pompeii_79.atrium.toy_note: Tucked under the horse, a note in a careful hand: "The diggers take what shines. I leave what a child hid. Some things are kept by being left where they were."
pompeii_79.lens.cloud: Over Vesuvius a cloud climbs straight up, higher than any cloud should, and spreads at the top like [[pine_tree]]. People in the street stop and look.
pompeii_79.lens.notice: The same notice, fresh and red: the bakers ask you to vote for their man. The paint is hardly a year old.
pompeii_79.lens.shop: The shop is open. Loaves are stacked on the counter, and the baker's boy is shutting the shutters early.
pompeii_79.lens.street_people: Three passers-by, faces turned up to the mountain. One has dropped a basket. Pale stones begin to tick on the paving.
pompeii_79.lens.mill: A donkey, blindfolded, stands still at the mill. No one has told it to walk on.
pompeii_79.lens.oven: The oven is sealed and hot, full of the day's bread. It will not be taken out.
pompeii_79.lens.basket: A basket of fresh loaves, each scored into eight, each stamped FELICIS: [[felix]]'s. Beside it, [[autumn]] fruit: pomegranates, chestnuts, a jug of the new wine.
pompeii_79.lens.shrine: A woman wraps the little bronze gods in a cloth. Then she presses a stone behind the painted panel, lays the strongbox key in the hollow, and slides the stone back. "We will come back for it."
pompeii_79.lens.basin: Stones patter down through the opening in the roof and bob in the basin: [[pumice]], so light it floats.
pompeii_79.lens.niche: Under the stair, a small hand pushes a clay horse on wheels deep into the niche, out of sight. It is too big to carry.
pompeii_79.lens.family: By the door, a man and a small child, [[pillows]] tied on their heads with cloth. The child looks back at the wall, a stick of charcoal in her hand.
pompeii_79.lens.fig: The fig tree still has late fruit. The vine above it has been picked bare: the harvest is in.
pompeii_79.garden.section: Where the diggers cut down through the garden, the ground shows its layers like pages. At the bottom, the old garden soil. Above it, nearly three metres of pale [[pumice]], the stones that fell all afternoon and all night. On top, a band of fine grey ash, set hard: [[surge]] that swept the city at [[dawn]] the next morning.
pompeii_79.garden.hollow: A hollow in the ash where a tree once stood. Its roots drank here for years before the stones came.
pompeii_79.garden.vesuvius: From the garden the mountain looks close enough to touch. It smokes, quietly, as if nothing had happened.
pompeii_79.label.done: The label is written. The house is empty because its people had time to leave. The lava and the single instant can stay in the guidebook.
pompeii_79.ending.autumn: For centuries the books said 24 August. The house remembered autumn: pomegranates, chestnuts, new wine sealed in its jars. In 2018 a line of charcoal on a wall nearby, dated mid-October, made many historians agree.
pompeii_79.ending.family: No one knows if Felix and his family found a boat. The house kept their bread, and a child's drawing of the sea.
item.pompeii_79.era_lens.name: Brass lens
item.pompeii_79.era_lens.desc: Through it the ash is not there yet. Raise it with the lens at the bottom left, and drag to look around.
item.pompeii_79.shovel.name: Shovel
item.pompeii_79.shovel.desc: A digger's shovel, its edge worn bright.
item.pompeii_79.tracings.name: Tracings
item.pompeii_79.tracings.desc: Four sheets of tracing paper, each with part of a drawing and a small cross at every corner.
hint.pompeii_79.start.1: The street is buried. The diggers' hut across the way might have what you need.
hint.pompeii_79.start.2: In the hut, take the shovel by the door and the lens on the drafting table.
hint.pompeii_79.dig.1: The shop door is under a bank of ash.
hint.pompeii_79.dig.2: Use the shovel on the ash bank.
hint.pompeii_79.trace.1: The tracings belong on the draughtsman's table in the hut.
hint.pompeii_79.trace.2: Use the tracings on the drafting table.
hint.pompeii_79.tracings.1: Each sheet has a cross at every corner, and so does the table.
hint.pompeii_79.tracings.2: Tap a sheet to turn it upright, then drag it over the crosses on the table.
hint.pompeii_79.tracings.3: Turn the figures three times, the words once and the gate twice; lay all four in the middle.
hint.pompeii_79.jar_label.1: The wax tablet names the baker and his gate.
hint.pompeii_79.jar_label.2: The garden's cut tells when those who stayed were caught.
whitechapel_1888.frames.empty: Five empty frames, each with a date on a brass plate. Under each, a strip of paper waits for a name and a place.
hint.whitechapel_1888.leave.1: The door is open now. The tale is written; you may go.
hint.whitechapel_1888.street_thread.1: Five streets, five pins. The thread must pass through them in order.
hint.whitechapel_1888.street_thread.2: The clippings on the desk are pinned oldest first.
hint.whitechapel_1888.street_thread.3: Buck's Row, Hanbury Street, Berner Street, Mitre Square, Miller's Court.
item.pompeii_79.arca_key.name: Bronze key
item.pompeii_79.arca_key.desc: A heavy bronze key with a ring for a finger, green with age. It was hidden, not lost.
item.pompeii_79.wax_tablet.name: Wax tablets
item.pompeii_79.wax_tablet.desc: Two wooden tablets hinged with cord, their wax gone dark and cracked. Something was written in them, but in daylight the strokes are too faint to read.
pompeii_79.atrium.fresco_fallen: The painted panel at the back of the shrine has fallen. Its pieces lie in the ash at your feet, the paint still bright on some of them.
pompeii_79.atrium.fresco_restored: The last piece settles. The panel is whole: the spirit of the house pouring an offering, two dancing gods, a serpent at the altar. Behind it, one stone sits loose.
pompeii_79.atrium.fresco_whole: The panel is whole again. One stone behind it sits loose, as if someone once moved it, but it will not come out for guessing. Whoever loosened it knew where to press.
pompeii_79.atrium.key_found: You press where she pressed. The stone slides out, and in the hollow behind the painted gods lies a bronze key.
pompeii_79.atrium.arca_locked: A strongbox of wood bound in iron, too heavy to carry off. The diggers wrote "locked, no key" in their day-book.
pompeii_79.atrium.arca_opened: The key turns stiffly. The money is gone, as the diggers thought, but at the bottom lie two wax tablets, tied with cord.
pompeii_79.atrium.arca_empty: The strongbox stands open and empty.
pompeii_79.atrium.drawing_traced: The drawing Felix wrote of, low on the wall by the door. Almost nothing of it is left, but the diggers' draughtsman traced it. His tin tube lies by the wall.
pompeii_79.lens.fresco: In the morning light the painted panel is whole and bright: the spirit of the house pouring an offering, two dancing gods with drinking horns, and below them a serpent coming to the altar.
pompeii_79.lens.child: A small child pulls a clay horse on wheels round and round the basin. Nobody tells her to stop.
pompeii_79.lens.basin_morning: Rainwater in the basin, clear as glass. A fig leaf turns slowly on it.
pompeii_79.lens.family_noon: The household stands in the atrium, faces turned up to the opening in the roof. Nobody speaks.
pompeii_79.hut.lamp: A clay oil lamp, lit, for reading in the dim of the hut. Its flame lies low and steady.
pompeii_79.hut.lamp_done: The lamp burns on. The tablets have given up what they held.
pompeii_79.hut.tablet_read: The light slides low across the wax, and the strokes stand up out of it, in a hand that pressed hard: "[[felix]] to his brother Rufus. The stones are falling. We are going down to the sea, out by [[marina_gate]], to find a boat. The little one has drawn you the way on the wall by the door, in case you come."
pompeii_79.label.seal: {1} the baker led his family out through {2}; those who stayed were taken at {3}.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco.1: The painted panel of the household shrine lies in pieces. Tap the shrine.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco.2: The lens shows the house before the ash. Turn it to the morning, and look at the shrine: the panel is whole there.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco.3: Tap a piece to turn it upright, then drag it into its place. The lens's morning picture shows where each belongs.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco_puzzle.1: Six pieces. Some lie upside down or sideways: tap a piece to turn it.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco_puzzle.2: The spirit of the house stands in the middle, the serpent at the bottom, the two gods at the sides.
hint.pompeii_79.fresco_puzzle.3: Turn every piece until its paint is upright, then lay them in two columns of three: head and shoulders at the top, altar and serpent at the bottom.
hint.pompeii_79.find_key.1: A stone behind the panel is loose, but only someone who saw it moved knows where to press.
hint.pompeii_79.find_key.2: Raise the lens in the atrium and turn it to the afternoon. Watch the shrine.
hint.pompeii_79.find_key.3: Through the lens in the afternoon, tap the woman at the shrine; then tap the shrine in the ruin.
hint.pompeii_79.open_arca.1: The key fits something heavy in the atrium.
hint.pompeii_79.open_arca.2: Use the bronze key on the strongbox.
hint.pompeii_79.read_tablet.1: The writing in the wax is too faint in daylight. It wants a low light.
hint.pompeii_79.read_tablet.2: Use the tablets on the oil lamp in the diggers' hut.
hint.pompeii_79.wax_tablet.1: Marks in wax show best when light grazes them from one side.
hint.pompeii_79.wax_tablet.2: Move the lamp slowly round the tablet and watch the strokes darken.
hint.pompeii_79.wax_tablet.3: Bring the lamp round to the left of the tablet, a little above the middle, and hold it there.
hint.pompeii_79.find_drawing.1: Felix wrote that the little one drew the way on the wall by the door.
hint.pompeii_79.find_drawing.2: The drawing is in the atrium, low on the wall. The draughtsman's tube lies beneath it.
hint.pompeii_79.seal.1: The seal waits at the household shrine in the atrium.
hint.pompeii_79.seal.2: Who led them out, which gate they took, and when the burning cloud came.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.path_unseen: The beam passes high over the yard. Down here the path west is still dark. From the gallery at the top of the tower you could see the whole island.
flannan_isles_1900.yard.rail_moved: You know now what lies across the path: a rail torn from the tramway. You drag it aside. The way west is open.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.gallery: A small iron door opens onto the gallery round the lantern. The wind takes your breath. Below, the island lies dark, and the beam goes round over it.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.gallery_done: From the gallery the beam goes round and round over the island. You have seen what it shows.
flannan_isles_1900.lamp.gallery_dark: A small iron door leads out onto the gallery. Out there it is black; there is nothing to see until the lamp is lit.
flannan_isles_1900.beam.rail: A rail across the path west
flannan_isles_1900.beam.turf: Turf torn from the cliff top
flannan_isles_1900.beam.crane: The crane at the west landing
flannan_isles_1900.beam.done: Each time the beam comes round you see it again: a rail torn from the tramway lying across the path west, the turf ripped from the top of the cliff, and far below, the crane at the west landing.
flannan_isles_1900.west.steps: Steps cut in the rock run down to the landing, where the sea is breaking. The waves come in sets. Watch them before you go down.
flannan_isles_1900.west.steps_done: The steps run down to the landing. You have been down once, between two seas; once is enough.
flannan_isles_1900.west.landing: At the foot of the steps the rock is scoured bare, and a block of stone that must weigh a ton has been shifted. Two men sent down to make the stores fast in a gale would go together, dressed for the sea in oilskins and seaboots. What came up these steps was [[great_sea]].
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.hooks_roster: The three hooks again. You know now where the men went. Set it down, man by man: his post, what he wore, and when he went.
flannan_isles_1900.kitchen.hooks_done: Three hooks, three men. Two went down dressed for the sea; the third ran after them without his coat.
flannan_isles_1900.roster.done: The roster is right. Ducat and Marshall went down first, dressed for the sea, to make the stores fast. McArthur ran after them in his shirtsleeves. No one knows why he went without his coat; perhaps he saw the sea coming.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.watch_beam.1: The light is back. From high up, you could see the whole island by it.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.watch_beam.2: In the lamp room, go out through the small iron door onto the gallery.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.go_down.1: Something happened down at the west landing. Go and see.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.go_down.2: Take the steps down to the landing, between the waves.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.who_went.1: The hooks by the kitchen door mean more now.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.who_went.2: Tap the hooks and set down each man's post, what he wore, and when he went.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.beam.1: Things out there show only while the beam is on them.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.beam.2: Watch where the beam falls, and tap just as it passes.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.beam.3: Three things: the rail on the path, the torn turf at the top of the cliff, the crane at the landing. Tap each while it is lit.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.swell.1: The waves come in a pattern. Watch a few before you go.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.swell.2: Before a great sea the water draws far back, with a rising roar.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.swell.3: Wait at the top. Go down steadily right after the great sea breaks.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.roster.1: The log says who signed as Principal, and who was only standing in.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.roster.2: The oilskin left behind hangs on one man's hook. A man who leaves his coat in a gale is in a hurry: he went after the others.
hint.flannan_isles_1900.roster.3: Ducat: Principal, oilskins, first. Marshall: Second Assistant, oilskins, first. McArthur: Occasional, shirtsleeves, after.
episode.bastille_1703.title: Bastille, 1703
episode.bastille_1703.teaser: A black velvet mask on a table, and a grave under another man's name.
item.bastille_1703.key_ring.name: Turnkey's keys
item.bastille_1703.key_ring.desc: A heavy iron ring of keys, each bit cut its own way.
item.bastille_1703.worksheet.name: Bazeries's worksheet
item.bastille_1703.worksheet.desc: Pencilled columns of numbers and syllables, dated 1893. It should not be here yet.
bastille_1703.courtyard.key_ring: On a nail by the tower door hangs the turnkey's ring of keys. No one has come for it this morning.
bastille_1703.courtyard.gate_shut: The gate to the street is barred. Outside, the parish of Saint-Paul is waking.
bastille_1703.courtyard.cart: A cart waits by the wall with a plain box on it. It will leave this afternoon.
bastille_1703.courtyard.towers: Eight towers close the court in. Beyond them, the bell of Saint-Paul.
bastille_1703.junca.journal: The journal of the King's lieutenant, Étienne du Junca. On [[date_1698]], Monsieur de Saint-Mars came to govern the Bastille, bringing a prisoner he had kept for years, always masked, in [[black_velvet]]. The newest line is still wet: on [[date_19nov]] the unknown prisoner died. He is to be buried this afternoon at Saint-Paul.
bastille_1703.junca.keeper_note: Between the pages for November, a slip in the keeper's hand: "Some names are taken on purpose, and some by a clerk's carelessness. He lost his twice: once to a mask, once to a spelling. I kept what was left."
bastille_1703.junca.journal_done: Du Junca's journal, open at November 1703.
bastille_1703.junca.worksheet: On the shelf, a sheet that should not be here yet: columns of numbers and syllables in pencil, signed Commandant Étienne Bazeries, 1893. It is a key to the king's Great Cipher.
bastille_1703.junca.window: From this window the King's lieutenant could see every door in the court.
bastille_1703.junca.candle: The candle has burned down in the night.
bastille_1703.office.letter_1669: A letter from the Marquis de Louvois to Monsieur de Saint-Mars, 19 July [[date_1669]]: a prisoner named [[eustache_dauger]] is coming to Pignerol. He is to be kept alone and to speak of nothing but his needs, on pain of death. And since he is only [[valet]], he needs little furniture.
bastille_1703.office.cipher_unread: Another letter, from 1691, written all in groups of numbers: the king's Great Cipher. Without its key it cannot be read.
bastille_1703.office.cipher_open: The numbers, and beside them the pencilled worksheet.
bastille_1703.office.cipher_read: Read, it is Louvois to General Catinat, 1691: arrest [[bulonde]], who lifted the siege of Cuneo, and take him to Pignerol, to be locked up at night and to walk the battlements by day "with a 330 309". Those two numbers are on no worksheet. In 1893 Bazeries guessed that they meant a mask. No key the king's ciphers used has that word.
bastille_1703.office.cipher_done: The 1691 letter, read but for two numbers.
bastille_1703.office.file_wait: The prisoner's file. It is thin: not everything about him is in it yet.
bastille_1703.office.file_open: Every paper about him, laid out on the governor's desk.
bastille_1703.office.file_sorted: Sorted, the file says less than the legends, and more. The papers written while he lived speak of a valet, a closed chair, a mask of black velvet, and a name in a register. None of them speaks of iron, or of a twin.
bastille_1703.office.file_done: The file, sorted: what was seen, and what was told.
bastille_1703.office.fire: The governor's fire is out. The ashes are cold.
bastille_1703.stair.door_locked: The tower door opens on a stair and, a little way up, a locked door. Without the turnkey's keys you will go no further.
bastille_1703.stair.door_lower: A heavy door bound in iron. The keyhole is cut to one key's shape.
bastille_1703.stair.door_lower_opened: The lock turns with a clack that climbs the stair. Above, another door.
bastille_1703.stair.door_upper_far: Higher up, another door. First, the one in front of you.
bastille_1703.stair.door_upper: A second door, heavier than the first. His cells always lay behind more than one.
bastille_1703.stair.door_upper_opened: The second lock gives. The door swings in on the third chamber of the Bertaudière.
bastille_1703.stair.steps: The steps are worn hollow in the middle by three centuries of feet.
bastille_1703.cell.mask: On the table lies a mask of [[black_velvet]]. You lift it: it weighs almost nothing. Not iron: cloth, stiffened, with strings to tie it. His face is not here to see.
bastille_1703.cell.seal_needed: Beside the mask, a blank order. Only what is known may be written on it.
bastille_1703.cell.bed: The bed has been stripped. Later accounts say his things were burned, and the walls of his cell scraped and whitewashed.
bastille_1703.cell.window: Bars across a narrow window. The dawn is grey over the roofs of the Faubourg Saint-Antoine.
bastille_1703.cell.voltaire: On the sill, a book that should not be here yet: Voltaire, 1751. It says the prisoner wore a mask of [[iron]], with steel springs at the chin so that he could eat.
bastille_1703.cell.walls: Stone, and the marks of damp. Nothing written, nothing scratched.
bastille_1703.paul.register: In the vestry of Saint-Paul the clerk is writing the day's burials: "[[marchioly]], aged about forty-five, died in the Bastille; buried the 20th." The name looks like [[mattioli]], an Italian once held by Saint-Mars. But Mattioli died on Sainte-Marguerite in 1694.
bastille_1703.paul.dumas: On a pew, a novel that should not be here yet: Alexandre Dumas. In it the masked prisoner is Louis XIV's secret brother, [[twin]].
bastille_1703.paul.window: Through the window, the churchyard of Saint-Paul, and a grave freshly dug.
bastille_1703.paul.candles: Candles for the dead of the parish.
bastille_1703.file.louvois_1669.title: Louvois to Saint-Mars, 1669
bastille_1703.file.louvois_1669.text: A prisoner named Eustache Dauger is coming. He is only a valet: he needs little furniture.
bastille_1703.file.saintmars_1687.title: Saint-Mars, 1687
bastille_1703.file.saintmars_1687.text: Carried to the island in a chair covered with oilcloth, twelve days on the road; it nearly killed him.
bastille_1703.file.bulonde_1691.title: Pignerol, 1691
bastille_1703.file.bulonde_1691.text: General Bulonde, held from 10 July; released by the king's order on 11 December.
bastille_1703.file.junca_1698.title: Du Junca's journal, 1698
bastille_1703.file.junca_1698.text: An old prisoner arrives with Monsieur de Saint-Mars, always masked, in black velvet.
bastille_1703.file.register_1703.title: Register of Saint-Paul, 1703
bastille_1703.file.register_1703.text: Marchioly, aged about forty-five, died in the Bastille; buried 20 November.
bastille_1703.file.voltaire.title: Voltaire, a history
bastille_1703.file.voltaire.text: The mask was iron, with steel springs at the chin.
bastille_1703.file.dumas.title: Alexandre Dumas, a novel
bastille_1703.file.dumas.text: He was Philippe, the king's twin, hidden so that no one would see the likeness.
bastille_1703.file.bazeries.title: Commandant Bazeries
bastille_1703.file.bazeries.text: The numbers 330 309 must mean "mask". The prisoner was General Bulonde.
bastille_1703.label.s1: The prisoner in the {1} mask, buried as {2}, is the man the letters call {3}.
bastille_1703.label.done: The order is written and sealed. It sends no one to prison. It only says what is known.
bastille_1703.ending.bell: The bell of Saint-Paul. He was buried that afternoon, under a name that was not the one in the letters.
bastille_1703.ending.names: Who he was, and why his face was hidden for thirty-four years, no one knows. The letters called him Eustache Dauger. His mask was black velvet.
hint.bastille_1703.start.1: The court has four doors: the tower, the King's lieutenant, the governor, and the street.
hint.bastille_1703.start.2: Take the turnkey's keys from the nail by the tower door, and read what the officers wrote.
hint.bastille_1703.climb_tower.1: The keys are for the Bertaudière, the tower on the left.
hint.bastille_1703.climb_tower.2: Climb to the third chamber. Each door takes one key.
hint.bastille_1703.read_cipher.1: The 1691 letter is in numbers. Someone, much later, worked out what they meant.
hint.bastille_1703.read_cipher.2: With Bazeries's worksheet, tap the letter on the governor's desk.
hint.bastille_1703.find_register.1: Du Junca wrote where he is to be buried today.
hint.bastille_1703.find_register.2: The street gate is open now: go to Saint-Paul and read the register.
hint.bastille_1703.sort_file.1: Everything you found is in the file on the governor's desk now.
hint.bastille_1703.sort_file.2: Tap the file and sort the papers: written while he lived, or told after.
hint.bastille_1703.write_seal.1: The mask waits on the cell table, and beside it a blank order.
hint.bastille_1703.write_seal.2: Write only what the record says.
hint.bastille_1703.door_lower.1: The keyhole is the shape of the key's bit.
hint.bastille_1703.door_lower.2: Find the key whose cuts match the keyhole exactly.
hint.bastille_1703.door_upper.1: The keyhole is the shape of the key's bit.
hint.bastille_1703.door_upper.2: One key matches, but only turned the other way round.
hint.bastille_1703.door_upper.3: The third key on the ring, turned over.
hint.bastille_1703.cipher.1: Each number is a syllable. Look it up on the worksheet.
hint.bastille_1703.cipher.2: Tap a number in the letter, then the same number on the worksheet. Two numbers are on no worksheet at all.
hint.bastille_1703.cipher.3: Bu-lon-de, Pi-gne-rol, les en-ne-mi-s, a-vec un… and then 330 309, which no one can read.
hint.bastille_1703.file.1: Which of these papers were written by people who saw him, while he lived?
hint.bastille_1703.file.2: Voltaire's history came out in 1751, Dumas was born in 1802, Bazeries worked in 1893. They could only repeat, or guess.
hint.bastille_1703.file.3: At the time: Louvois 1669, Saint-Mars 1687, Pignerol 1691, du Junca 1698, the register 1703. Afterwards: Voltaire, Dumas, Bazeries.
hint.bastille_1703.jar_label.1: What was the mask made of, in the journal of the man who saw it?
hint.bastille_1703.jar_label.2: Under what name was he buried, and what name do the 1669 letters give?
episode.gyeongju_771.title: Gyeongju, 771
episode.gyeongju_771.teaser: A great bell in the snow, and a legend that gave it a child's voice.
item.gyeongju_771.striker_rope.name: Hemp rope
item.gyeongju_771.striker_rope.desc: New rope, thick as a wrist. Strong enough to hang a log from.
gyeongju_771.yard.tally: By the gate, the founders' board, with the names the bell's inscription will carry. Chief founder, of the tenth rank: [[park_jong_il]]. Under him, Park Bin-na and Park Han-mi, of the eleventh, and Park Bu-ak, of the twelfth.
gyeongju_771.yard.keeper_note: Tucked behind the founders' board, a slip in the keeper's hand: "For a hundred years people listened to this bell for a child. Four men had put their names on it, and no one read them. I have written them down again."
gyeongju_771.yard.tally_done: The founders' board: Park Jong-il, Park Bin-na, Park Han-mi, Park Bu-ak.
gyeongju_771.yard.pavilion_empty: The bell pavilion stands ready, its great beam empty. The bell is still in the ground, in its mould.
gyeongju_771.yard.lanterns: Paper lanterns in the snow. It is the fourteenth day of the twelfth month.
gyeongju_771.shed.plan: Scratched on a board, the plan of the channels: from three furnaces, clay runs down to the mould's three pouring cups. The bronze must reach every cup, and spill nowhere.
gyeongju_771.shed.rope: A coil of new hemp rope, thick as a wrist. The log that will strike the bell needs two ropes to hang from.
gyeongju_771.shed.story_1925: On the bench, a newspaper that should not be here yet: the Maeil Sinbo of [[date_1925]]. A children's story: [[child]] is cast into a bell, and the bell cries [[emille]] for its mother. It is the first time the name is printed.
gyeongju_771.shed.tools: Ladles with long handles, tongs, scrapers for the clay. The founders' tools, cold for now.
gyeongju_771.shed.clay: Clay and wax. The bell's patterns were modelled before the mould was made: the lotus bosses, the kneeling celestials, the dragon on the crown.
gyeongju_771.pit.mould: The mould lies in a pit in the ground, bound and packed. Channels of clay run to it from the furnaces.
gyeongju_771.pit.mould_done: The pit is empty but for broken mould and cooling sand.
gyeongju_771.pit.furnaces: Three furnaces glow. The bronze in them is ready. It has taken years, and two kings, to come to this night.
gyeongju_771.pit.channels: Clay channels, each piece set loose in the sand. They can be turned.
gyeongju_771.pit.poured: The furnaces open. Bronze runs down the channels into every cup, and the mould drinks it.
gyeongju_771.pit.raised: When it has cooled, the mould is broken away. The bell is raised to the pavilion, whole.
gyeongju_771.hall.draft: On the desk, the draft of the inscription by [[kim_pil_o]]. In memory of the great [[seongdeok]], the bell was begun by his son and finished by his grandson, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month of [[date_771]]. Its sound, he writes, is the perfect voice of the Buddha's teaching, for all who suffer to hear. At the end, the names of those who made it: chief founder [[park_jong_il]] and three founders under him.
gyeongju_771.hall.hulbert: On a shelf, a book that should not be here yet: Homer Hulbert, The Passing of Korea, 1906. In it, a great bell will not ring until [[child]] is cast into its metal. His bell hangs in [[seoul]], not here.
gyeongju_771.hall.window: Snow on the temple roofs. Far off, the round tombs of Silla's kings.
gyeongju_771.hall.lamp: An oil lamp, turned low, for the one who writes late.
gyeongju_771.pav.striker_loose: The log striker hangs by one rope. Its other end rests on a trestle.
gyeongju_771.pav.rope_tied: You tie the new rope to the beam. The log hangs level, its end towards the lotus on the bell.
gyeongju_771.pav.striker: The log hangs ready. Below the bell's mouth, a hollow is dug in the ground.
gyeongju_771.pav.striker_done: The bell rings. The sound swells and fades, and swells again, long after the log is still.
gyeongju_771.pav.bell_silent: The bell hangs by its dragon hook, the sound tube beside it. It has not yet been struck.
gyeongju_771.pav.bell_rim: You kneel under the rim. Strike it all the way round, and watch how the ring rises and falls.
gyeongju_771.pav.seal_needed: A chalk cross on the rim marks where the [[beat]] swells deepest. Paper and ink wait by the inscription, to take a rubbing.
gyeongju_771.pav.report: Under the eaves, a paper that should not be here yet, from 1998: the Gyeongju National Museum had the bell's metal analysed. No phosphorus was found, the main element of bone. Nothing of [[child]] is in it.
gyeongju_771.pav.hollow: A [[hollow]] in the ground under the bell's mouth. Korean bells hang over one; it holds the sound.
gyeongju_771.pav.apsaras: On the bell, celestials kneel on clouds, holding censers, facing the lotus where the log strikes.
gyeongju_771.pav.first_ring: The log swings, and the bell speaks for the first time. The sound goes on and on, over the snow.
gyeongju_771.pav.hollow_found: Over the right [[hollow]], the ring lasts longest: the ground answers the bronze.
gyeongju_771.pav.beat_found: There. The bell's tone is not one tone but two, a hair apart, because the bronze is not quite even all round. Struck here, the two sound equally, and swell and fade together: a [[beat]]. Later ears heard a child crying in it.
gyeongju_771.label.s1: Cast in {1} by {2} and three founders, the bell holds no child: its cry is the {3} of its bronze.
gyeongju_771.label.done: The rubbing is taken. On the black paper, the names stand out pale.
gyeongju_771.ending.ring: The bell rang for more than twelve hundred years: from a temple, then a city gate, then a museum. Since 1992 it has been struck only now and then, to test its voice.
gyeongju_771.ending.names: Its founders put their names on it: Park Jong-il, Park Bin-na, Park Han-mi, Park Bu-ak. The cry was never a child's.
hint.gyeongju_771.start.1: The founders' board by the gate names who is casting the bell.
hint.gyeongju_771.start.2: The bell is still in its mould, in the pit. The furnaces are ready.
hint.gyeongju_771.find_rope.1: The bell hangs in the pavilion, but its log striker has only one rope.
hint.gyeongju_771.find_rope.2: The founders keep rope in their shed.
hint.gyeongju_771.tie_rope.1: Use the rope on the striker in the pavilion.
hint.gyeongju_771.ring_bell.1: Strike the bell with the log.
hint.gyeongju_771.ring_bell.2: Pull hard, and mind the hollow under the bell.
hint.gyeongju_771.find_cry.1: Listen to how the ring swells and fades. Where does that come from?
hint.gyeongju_771.find_cry.2: Tap the bell to kneel under its rim, and strike it all the way round.
hint.gyeongju_771.write_seal.1: The bell waits to be written: when it was cast, by whom, and what its cry is.
hint.gyeongju_771.write_seal.2: Tap the bell in the pavilion.
hint.gyeongju_771.pour.1: The bronze must reach every cup, and run nowhere else.
hint.gyeongju_771.pour.2: The middle furnace runs straight down. The outer two turn inwards at the middle row.
hint.gyeongju_771.pour.3: Left furnace: down, right, down into the first cup. Middle: straight down. Right furnace: down, left, down into the last cup. Leave the rest.
hint.gyeongju_771.resonance.1: Pull the log far back: a gentle pull barely rings the bell.
hint.gyeongju_771.resonance.2: Change the hollow between strikes. The ring lasts longest over one depth only.
hint.gyeongju_771.resonance.3: Dig three times from the start, and pull the log all the way back.
hint.gyeongju_771.beat.1: Strike every place, and watch the trace: how far does it dip between swells?
hint.gyeongju_771.beat.2: Where the swell is deepest, the ring almost falls silent between its waves.
hint.gyeongju_771.beat.3: The place at the lower left of the rim.
hint.gyeongju_771.jar_label.1: When was the bell finished, and who cast it? The inscription says.
hint.gyeongju_771.jar_label.2: What makes it sound like crying? You found it under the rim.
episode.whitechapel_1891.title: Whitechapel, 1891
episode.whitechapel_1891.teaser: A new black hat under a railway arch, and a file that holds more names than anyone remembers.
whitechapel_1891.station.book: The occurrence book of H Division. The newest entry is PC Ernest Thompson's: at 2.15 a.m. on [[date_13feb]], passing under the railway arch at [[swallow_gardens]], he heard a man's footsteps walking away, and found a woman lying there, still alive. Regulations kept him with her. He blew his whistle, and the constables of the next beats came running. She did not survive. Her name was [[frances_coles]].
whitechapel_1891.station.seal_needed: The file's cover waits for its last entry.
whitechapel_1891.station.street_shut: The street door. First, read what the night has brought in.
whitechapel_1891.station.file_locked: The file room is locked. The inspector with the key is out, and the reporters with him.
whitechapel_1891.station.charge_sheet: A charge sheet that should not be here yet: on 16 February, [[sadler]], a ship's fireman who had spent her last days with her, will be charged with her murder, and at the start of March released. Nothing linked him to it.
whitechapel_1891.station.notices: Yellowed bills from 1888 still on the board, asking for information. They are three years old.
whitechapel_1891.station.lamp: The gas burns low. It is past three in the morning.
whitechapel_1891.arch.arch: The arch runs under the railway, dark and wet. Somewhere ahead, footsteps walking away. Then nothing.
whitechapel_1891.arch.hat: On the cobbles lies a new hat of black crêpe, bought the evening before. Tucked in its band, a milliner's ticket: Nottingham Street.
whitechapel_1891.arch.chalk: A constable's chalk mark on the stones, where she was found.
whitechapel_1891.arch.lamp: One gas lamp at the mouth of the arch. Its light does not reach far.
whitechapel_1891.arch.corner: Round the corner, the streets towards Nottingham Street. Nothing leads there yet.
whitechapel_1891.arch.train: A goods train crosses overhead, and the arch shakes with it.
whitechapel_1891.arch.cab_early: A reporter's cab, already. The driver says the papers will have it by morning.
whitechapel_1891.shop.order_book: The milliner's order book, left open on the counter. Thursday evening, about half past seven: one black crêpe hat. The police would learn that the money for it came from [[sadler]].
whitechapel_1891.shop.hats: Hats on stands and in boxes: straw for the spring, felt and crêpe for now.
whitechapel_1891.shop.window: The shutters are up. The street outside is empty.
whitechapel_1891.shop.crepe: A roll of black crêpe, the same as on her new hat.
whitechapel_1891.press.forme: The forme for the morning's front page, locked up and inked. The headline is set in the largest type: JACK THE RIPPER AGAIN? Her name is nowhere in it.
whitechapel_1891.press.forme_done: The headline carries her name now, in the largest type the case holds.
whitechapel_1891.press.spike: On the spike, a copy of an old letter: "Dear Boss", sent to the Central News Agency in September 1888 and signed [[jack]]. It gave the killer the name. Pinned to it, a note that should not be here yet: in 1913 John Littlechild, once head of Special Branch, called the letter "a smart piece of journalistic work".
whitechapel_1891.press.case: The type case: capitals above, small letters below, every letter cut backwards in the metal.
whitechapel_1891.press.press: The press waits for the forme. By six the papers will be on the street.
whitechapel_1891.press.name_set: The line is set: FRANCES COLES. Whatever the morning calls the killer, it will print her name.
whitechapel_1891.file.shelf: The shelf of the Whitechapel Murders file. Five files stand on it, as people will remember them. Look away, and the shelf will not stay as it is.
whitechapel_1891.file.shelf_done: Eleven files, from April 1888 to February 1891.
whitechapel_1891.file.docket: The file's cover sheet: Whitechapel Murders. Opened in April 1888, with [[emma_smith]].
whitechapel_1891.file.keeper_note: Inside the cover, in the keeper's careful hand: "The first jar kept five names in the small print. This one keeps the whole file. Count them: eleven."
whitechapel_1891.file.docket_done: The cover sheet, and the keeper's slip inside it.
whitechapel_1891.file.memo: A paper that should not be here yet: a memorandum by Melville Macnaghten, dated [[date_1894]]. "The Whitechapel Murderer had 5 victims, & 5 victims only", from [[mary_ann_nichols]] to [[mary_jane_kelly]]. It stayed private until the 1950s. Then the world counted [[five]].
whitechapel_1891.file.lamp: The lamp gutters whenever you look away from the shelf.
whitechapel_1891.file.whole: The file is whole: [[emma_smith]], Martha Tabram, Mary Ann Nichols, Annie Chapman, Elizabeth Stride, Catherine Eddowes, Mary Jane Kelly, Rose Mylett, Alice McKenzie, a woman who was never named, and [[frances_coles]]. [[eleven]] women.
whitechapel_1891.label.s1: From {1} to {2}, the file holds {3} women.
whitechapel_1891.label.done: The cover is written. Eleven names, in the file's own hand.
whitechapel_1891.ending.buried: Frances Coles was buried at East London Cemetery on 25 February 1891.
whitechapel_1891.ending.file: The file was never closed, and in it the eleven were never five. The name the papers gave the killer came from a letter the police thought a journalist wrote.
hint.whitechapel_1891.start.1: Read the night's entry in the occurrence book.
hint.whitechapel_1891.start.2: Then go out to Swallow Gardens.
hint.whitechapel_1891.find_ticket.1: Look closely at what lies under the arch.
hint.whitechapel_1891.find_ticket.2: The new hat has a milliner's ticket in its band.
hint.whitechapel_1891.milliner.1: The ticket names a shop in Nottingham Street.
hint.whitechapel_1891.milliner.2: From the arch, go round the corner to the milliner's.
hint.whitechapel_1891.set_name.1: The papers will have the story by morning. A reporter's cab waits by the arch.
hint.whitechapel_1891.set_name.2: In the composing room, the headline has no name. Set hers.
hint.whitechapel_1891.grow_file.1: The file room at Leman Street is open now.
hint.whitechapel_1891.grow_file.2: Look away from the shelf, and look back.
hint.whitechapel_1891.write_seal.1: The file's cover waits for its last entry.
hint.whitechapel_1891.write_seal.2: Tap the occurrence book at Leman Street.
hint.whitechapel_1891.compose.1: On a sort, the letter is cut backwards. Pick the sorts whose letters look backwards.
hint.whitechapel_1891.compose.2: Some sorts look right on their face: those print backwards. Watch the proof.
hint.whitechapel_1891.compose.3: For every letter take the mirrored sort, and the blank sort for the space.
hint.whitechapel_1891.unwatched.1: Before you look away, note what stands where.
hint.whitechapel_1891.unwatched.2: Only one file is new each time; others may have moved.
hint.whitechapel_1891.unwatched.3: They come in the order the file grew: Emma Smith, Martha Tabram, Rose Mylett, Alice McKenzie, an unknown woman, Frances Coles.
hint.whitechapel_1891.jar_label.1: Whose name opens the file, and whose closes it?
hint.whitechapel_1891.jar_label.2: How many women does the file hold? Not the memorandum: the file.
